trial_court: Family Court, Dhenkanal, C.P. No.67 of 2020 and C.P. No.29 of 2021
facts_of_case: Matrimonial suit filed by the appellant was dismissed observing that the suit is collusive one. The respondent was reluctant to bring out the truth by way of cross-examination.

legal_principles.principle: The requirement of leave to dispense with joinder must be observed in a suit for restitution of conjugal rights.
legal_principles.held: The Judge, Family Court has also observed that such rule is required to be observed in the proceeding under Section-9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, mutatis mutandis.

legal_principles.principle: The custody of a child should be decided based on the best interests of the child.
legal_principles.held: We had interaction with the parties being parents of the child and also with the child, Shaunak to understand the elements of comfort, assurance of proper care and bringing him up in a manner so that he can meet the challenges of life.

legal_principles.principle: The parties should not take any legal action against each other or their family members after the decree of divorce.
legal_principles.held: Both the parties undertake that in view of this compromise they will not take any legal action against either party or their family members, relating to their marital life, after passing of the decree of divorce.

outcome.final_order: The matrimonial suit stood dismissed on contest.

use_for_drafting: drafting a divorce appeal in Orissa High Court
advising on matrimonial disputes under Hindu Marriage Act
preparing a case for Family Courts Act
